subject: Pricing & Ramp: Nimbus Health multi-year commitment
messages:
From: Alyssa Grant <alyssa.grant@nimbushealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing / Ramp for multi-year prepay

Sean—thanks again for the demo yesterday. Nimbus is interested in a 3-year prepay commitment tied to our predictive care routing workload. A few constraints from procurement: we need an annual prepay (rather than monthly invoices), ability to ramp spend (we expect utilization to grow), and a single consolidated PO per year.

High-level ask from Nimbus:
- 3-year term, total committed $6.5M (roughly $2.0M / $2.2M / $2.3M across Y1-Y3)
- A term discount applied to the committed token unit price (they asked us for ~40% list-level discount)
- 30–60 day SLA credits, SOC2 + custom DPA are required

Procurement asked if you can accommodate a non-standard ramp (lower first-year consumption with make-good/burn-rate carry-forward into year 2) and a deeper term discount for the multi-year commit. They also flagged that Nimbus wants dedicated capacity for part of the workload and will require an onboarding credit if the ramp is slower.

Can you share a ballpark and let me know what approvals we need to get to a formal quote? I can loop in procurement and legal once we have a proposal.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Grant
VP, Strategic Partnerships
Nimbus Health

Attachment: Nimbus_LOI_signed.pdf (pdf)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa.grant@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing / Ramp for multi-year prepay

Alyssa—great to meet you yesterday. Appreciate the LOI and clarity on procurement constraints. High-level we can support a 3-year annual prepay with a ramp and make-good policy. I want to be transparent about what will require exec approval: the deep term discount (40% off list) and any guaranteed dedicated capacity plus onboarding credits.

Initial commercial direction (ballpark):
- Committed spend: $6.5M over 3 years (Y1 $2.0M, Y2 $2.2M, Y3 $2.3M)
- Proposed term discount: 28–32% off list depending on final commitment and payment terms
- Ramp policy: carry-forward up to 15% of unused commitment to year 2; additional carry-forward or onboarding credit requires exception
- Dedicated capacity surcharge: +9% of committed spend unless we design a shared-dedicated hybrid (can reduce surcharge but adds complexity)

I need to escalate to Marissa / Vivek for approval to go deeper (they'll need the usage forecast and LOI). Can you share the usage forecast (month-by-month) and any redline preferences on the DPA? If procurement is sensitive to a 40% ask, we'll need a strong justification (strategic value + referenceability + multi-region expansion plan).

I'll pull internal numbers and ping you within 48 hours.

Best,
Sean
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing / Ramp for multi-year prepay — exec approval requested

Folks—looping you on Nimbus Health (large strategic healthcare buyer). They're asking for a 3-year, $6.5M prepay with an aggressive 40% term discount request and a flexible ramp / carry-forward policy. Key commercial asks:
- 40% off list on committed units
- Allow carry-forward of unused Y1 commitment into Y2 (they propose unlimited carry-forward during onboarding)
- Dedicated capacity for a portion of workload (security/regulatory requirement)
- Onboarding credits if ramp slower than forecast

Why this matters: Nimbus is a potential platform reference in health segment, multi-region (US + EU) roadmap, and could expand into a dedicated capacity contract after year 1. If we win this commit and they become a reference, we expect an incremental 20–30% expansion opportunity.

Numbers: they've laid out $2.0M / $2.2M / $2.3M by year. My recommended concession envelope without further approval: up to 32% term discount, carry-forward cap at 15% of yearly commitment, and a one-time onboarding credit up to $80k. Anything beyond that needs exec OK.

Ask: Can we approve a 36–40% term discount and a more generous carry-forward (25–30%) if we get: (a) an expanded reference clause, (b) firm commitment to explore Dedicated conversion in Y2, and (c) acceptance of a 12-month ROI review clause? I attached the LOI and their high-level forecast they sent (usage-forecast.xlsx).

Thanks,
Sean

Attachments: Nimbus_LOI_signed.pdf, usage-forecast.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing / Ramp for multi-year prepay — exec approval requested

Sean—thanks for the summary. A few quick clarifying Qs before we consider an exception:
1) Is there an existing pilot or production usage today? The LOI suggests they are onboarding post-contract and expect a slow ramp in Q1.
2) What is the expected blended unit price at 32% vs 40% discount? Need absolute $/token to model CAC payback.
3) Are we ok with an unlimited carry-forward? My preference is a clear cap (we should avoid open-ended make-goods).
4) Is the dedicated capacity portion scoped? If it's >30% of compute, the economics change materially.

If Sean can provide the month-by-month forecast and a simple TCO table (list price vs 32% vs 40%), I'm willing to review with Vivek for an exception call. We should tie any extra concession to: public reference, a 12-month health check, and a fallback pricing clause if utilization deviates by >40% vs forecast.

-Marissa
VP Sales Operations

On 2026-11-30 Sean Gallagher wrote:
> Folks—looping you on Nimbus Health...

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing / Ramp for multi-year prepay — exec approval requested

Marissa—thanks. Attached is the month-by-month forecast and a simple TCO table comparing list / 32% / 40% scenarios. Key points:
- Current pilot: small internal proof-of-concept (non-production) — no billed usage today.
- Forecast (attached): slow ramp in Q1 Y1, with usage hitting ~70% of Y1 commitment by end of Q2; Y2 assumes 15% growth vs committed; Y3 assumes 4% growth.
- Blended unit price impact: list = $0.0012/token (example), 32% => $0.000816/token, 40% => $0.00072/token. At 40% the margin is thin but still positive with expected batching/quantization savings.

Proposed conditional exception (what we offer to Nimbus to close):
- 38% term discount applied to committed units (midpoint between our standard and their ask)
- Carry-forward cap at 25% of Y1 commitment into Y2 only (no multi-year unlimited carry)
- One-time onboarding credit up to $100k if actual Y1 usage < 60% of Y1 committed spend after 6 months
- Dedicated capacity: we will reserve a hybrid pool that represents up to 25% of their peak; surcharge +7% on that portion
- Requirements from Nimbus: public reference clause (case study within 9 months), agreement to a 12-month ROI review, and a commitment to evaluate Dedicated expansion in Y2 with a negotiating window locked at current rates for 60 days following the review.

I've attached: usage-forecast.xlsx and pricing-comparison.pdf. Requesting approval for the conditional exception (38% discount, 25% carry-forward cap, $100k onboarding credit, hybrid-dedicated at +7%).

Sean
Senior Account Executive

Attachments: usage-forecast.xlsx, pricing-comparison.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Approval: Nimbus Health conditional exception (38% / carry-forward / onboarding credit)

Team—after reviewing the LOI, forecast, and the strategic upside, I approve the conditional exception as proposed by Sean with the following binding conditions:
1) Discount capped at 38% on committed units; no retroactive increases.
2) Carry-forward limited to 25% of Y1 into Y2 only; unused credits expire at end of Y2.
3) Onboarding credit capped at $100k and applied only if Y1 usage <60% of committed spend after 6 months; credit will be paid as invoice credit, not cash.
4) Hybrid dedicated reservation (<=25% peak) at +7% surcharge; any dedicated >25% will revert to standard Dedicated economics and require a new approval.
5) Nimbus must sign a public reference clause (case study draft within 9 months) and commit to the 12-month ROI review. Failure to comply gives Redwood the right to revisit pricing at the ROI milestone.
6) Legal: include a 60-day renegotiation window post-ROI review to convert pricing to Dedicated economics if both parties agree.

Finance & Legal to model final quote and ensure margin floor and booking treatment. Sean—please push the updated term sheet to DocuSign with the conditions and copy Marissa and me. Once signed, we can move to procurement.

-Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer
